verification_report.summary:
The complete submitted chapter is correct under the stipulated accepted prerequisites. Thirteen sequential records check 90 deductions, and five reference/dependency records confirm the cited scopes and definitions. No critical error or gap was found. All four prerequisite reports are available and passed; the older conditional analytic dependency in intrinsic_trace_data_01 is resolved. The manuscript and supplied sources were read without modification.

The nonclosed removal lemma is valid: locally choose ddc rho>=beta, apply the closed-current restriction identity to T=ddc(w+rho), and use the fact that the smooth correction has zero coefficient mass on analytic sets. Subtraction leaves the positive coefficient-measure restriction to the complement. The exact identity is stated in Demailly, Lemma 2.17(b), and the supplied SGPT source confirms the compatible normalization. Theorem search was followed by primary-source web verification. [Demailly, Analytic Methods in Algebraic Geometry](https://www-fourier.ujf-grenoble.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/analmeth_book.pdf).

The image ideals give finite D_m on each compact model. Genuine analytic pullbacks and divisorial removal yield the linear Gauduchon bound; distributional Stokes uses only ddc(gamma^(r-1))=0, including the r=1 case. Finite-subset coefficient limits give the bound for every fixed Gauduchon metric. Positive divisor areas then give countable support and summability. Trace mass controls coefficient measures, so the increasing partial sums define a finite positive current; continuity of distributional differentiation proves it is closed. The supremum formula gives D_m<=S for every integer m, and the full integer limit with dominated convergence gives vanishing weighted total variation and weak current convergence. Ideal superadditivity gives dyadic increase. Only a tail of analytic approximants is needed.

Model compatibility is valid. Strict transforms preserve valuations and push forward with degree one; exceptional divisors push forward to zero because their restricted maps have rank at most r-2. Proper pushforward passes through the summable current series. Accepted coefficient additivity and real homogeneity give the corresponding current identities. For each finite divisor family, local Cartier divisibility pulls back as an inclusion of generated image ideals and gives the asserted order inequality. Taking its finite coefficient limit proves the pullback inequality without any claim about infinite pullback continuity.

One normalized subsequence of the restricted approximants converges on Y. Passing its curvature inequality to the limit places v in the original theta|_Y background. The accepted fixed-modification L1 lemma applies to that same subsequence on every subsequently fixed model. Pointwise Lelong upper semicontinuity, pointwise domination of generic orders, and the full integer trace limit give every required divisorial inequality without further extraction. Finite divisorial removal followed by the established current limit proves theta_Z+ddc(v composed with pi)>=S_Z. The proof asserts neither exact Lelong equality nor uniqueness, and uses no nonlinear mass convergence, BMP/PVP, or Bott-Chern class for nonclosed theta.
